199.s: His father was a gifted house-party pianist who preferred riverfront work and showed him only seventh chords.
199.q: years ago. Well, my dad, man, my dad was a hell of a piano player, man, but he'd rather work on a riverfront than a, he had a natural talent. And when he go to the house party, he'd upset the party, man. He and two other guys, they'd go around and they'd go to house parties and they'd be piano…

199.t: Growing up with a piano at home
199.s: There was always a piano among relatives; Cotton fooled around with boogie-woogie, and recalls a man who played only the black keys.
199.q: Would you consider yourself a piano player? Oh yeah, I always could play it man. I came up with the piano around in my house. We always had a piano. We always had a piano? We had a piano with my aunt, my grandmother, and my cousin. And where I went, they always had a piano then. And I'd get up…

770.t: Other instruments and dislike of piano
770.s: He can play the brass valve instruments and took some piano but found it a girl's instrument.
770.q: Well, I, I, I know the valve instruments. That's the trumpet and the baritone, and, uh, and, uh, the French horn and so forth. All, all the brass instruments I can play. And, uh, took a little piano from my mother, but, uh, I didn't care much for the piano. In those, uh, early years, uh, especially…

1040.t: Learning piano at his godmother's house
1040.s: He could only practice on his godmother's piano when her husband was not sleeping or she was in a good mood.
1040.q: Well, I'll tell you how that was. My godmother had a piano, see? And I could only get to play it whenever, you know, her husband wasn't sleeping, or if she was in a good mood, well, then I'd get a chance to play. But other than that, I couldn't get to the piano.

266.t: Piano and banjo at home, lessons
266.s: The only instruments at home were piano and banjo; everyone took lessons and Jones did not take to practice until later.
266.q: I'm trying to think. We had no other instruments at home other than the piano and that banjo. I didn't get my, I didn't play any other instrument or have any contact with any other instrument until I went to the military school. Yeah.

279.t: Learning piano from his mother and uncle
279.s: His mother taught him notes on the family upright, and his vaudeville uncle encouraged him; music was all he wanted.
279.q: I had no reason, John. John, I had no other reason but that I just loved this sound and I wanted to do it. I don't know. I can't say that I wanted to do it to prove anything. I just wanted to play it. And my mother had a piano. She had one of these old upright pianos.

176.s: She recalls early tunes like Bells That Ring for Me and My Gal and the blues, and her sister playing Keller's Love at home.
176.q: Well I didn't play much, I mean the general much around there no more. And I played at St. Carlos Hotel. What an orchestra band up there.

780.t: Church choir and teaching himself piano around age 12
780.s: His father sang in the church choir; Crawford taught himself piano with friends, not learning from anyone in particular.
780.q: No. Well, my father sung in the choir at church. And I did too for a while. Well, in fact I still do. But he never played music for a living.

802.t: Musical family, library home and rowboat rehearsals
802.s: His mother and grandmother taught piano but did not encourage him; raised in a Carnegie Library, he practiced cornet, banjo and mandolin along the river, self-taught.
802.q: Wouldn't allow me to play in the house You know Why, what was their attitude? Well, first of all, of course you know that I was raised in a Carnegie Library Oh

303.t: Childhood music: Handy, his father's fiddle and mother's ragtime
303.s: Hearing his brother's band, Handy dances, learning Over the Waves, losing his piano in a fire, his mother's training.
303.q: I see. She played the style, if you played what they call in those days was ragtime which was Scott Joplin style. She played Dill Pickle and Maple Leaf Rag and all those things. She had all the music to it. I've got the original music on Missouri Waltz and all those kind of things.

309.t: First instrument: piano and the organ blues his mother disliked
309.s: He first played piano and organ, sneaking blues on his mother's church organ while his sister watched for her.
309.ch: Early music and bands on the coast
309.q: No, alone. My mother, she had an organ and she used to play for the church. And, uh, I used to get up there and kind of fiddle around with the blues on the organ. And every time I started with the blues on the organ, she'd get a stick and run me off. But all we did not put the blues.

153.t: Drumming from age three, piano study, and teachers
153.s: Bellson describes his musical family, wanting to play drums after a parade, teachers Knapp, Spivak and Buddy Baker, and why his father steered him to piano; he notes drummers who also compose.
153.q: Actually no, see I come from a musical family. My father played all the instruments and had a music store, and there were eight of us, four girls, four boys, and all of us worked in the music store. And when I was about three and a half years old, my father took me to a parade, and you know for a…

130.t: Early piano lessons, perfect pitch and family support
130.s: Bushkin studied with a neighbour girl, was found to have perfect pitch by the landlord's son, and his father supported his music.
130.q: No I studied, when I was about nine or ten I studied with a girl who lived up on the third floor of an apartment building we lived in, and I enjoyed the 45 minutes or an hour once a week and learned to play the “Minuet in G” like all the kids, and the scales or whatever. © Hamilton College Jazz…

326.t: Mother's piano lessons and daily practice
326.s: His mother taught the children to read music and made them practice an hour a day in winter, two in summer.
326.q: And the piano training we had earlier was a real good introduction to music because my mother taught us all how to read music. She didn’t know a lot about it herself, she knew just like the basic value of the notes, a quarter note gets a beat, and then a few things like that. But she made us…

447.s: He and his brother took piano lessons because their father insisted.
447.q: Yeah. I started on piano. Both my brother and I took piano lessons when we were kids. My father insisted on it. And it’s the one thing that he really did for us — he insisted, no matter what we played he said it would give you a basis of understanding the music. My brother actually plays better…

141.t: Electricity at 13, the player piano and first piano lessons
141.s: No electricity until he was 13; his father learned from the player piano and Allison took lessons from age five.
141.q: Yeah. Well, the piano was in my grandfather’s house. My father learned how to play the piano from the wind-up....

703.s: His holy-roller aunt gave him piano lessons that ended when she announced the Holy Ghost was beside them.
703.q: Well, that’s a good one. Yeah. My aunt, Aunt Addie, who lived in Watts, which – she was a minister of the Holy Roller Church. It was one of those churches. It was in a tent. They would really get to going, where everybody was screaming and hollering and shaking, and everybody’s rolling around on…

526.t: First piano lessons, singing and biting her mother
526.s: She learned piano from both parents, played at church events, sang at three with a tin cup, and her mother stopped teaching after she bit her.
526.q: Well my father was a piano teacher, so I learned to play as I learned to walk, you know. It’s just so natural. My mother was also a musician, and gave me piano lessons.

504.t: First piano lessons with Antoinette Rich and Viola Burns
504.s: His grandmother starts him on piano at 5 or 6; a harsh first teacher is replaced by the friendly Viola Burns.
504.q: Yeah, well there was radio and in the area in those times there was, it wasn't unusual for you to study or take up piano. My grandmother knew a woman downtown named Antoinette Rich who had a studio their with spinet pianos, and she had students. My grandmother took me down to study, to start…

527.t: First piano lessons and copying his mother's hymns
527.s: His musical start with a visiting white piano teacher at grammar school and with his mother's choir practice.
527.q: Well actually, I began my musical career out of school because this was the time of the WPA, and everybody had a job. If you were a music teacher and you didn’t have a job, then they would give you a job teaching the kids. No, I’m jumping the gun. Actually, my music studying began in the grammar…

371.t: Starting piano lessons at ten, cost, and practice discipline
371.s: Lessons began at about 10-11 with the teacher coming to the house to teach his sisters and him in turn at $.75 each; his mother insisted on practice; his father only objected to jazz on Sundays and in church.
371.ch: Pontiac childhood, family and piano training
371.q: Well, I had been taking lessons from a beat – – it might have started when I was 10. Let's say 10 or 11 and 12, because by 13 I was already working in a small band.

16.s: He took on-and-off piano lessons from age 4; his mother took him to hear Paderewski play Minuet in G at Madison Square Garden.
16.q: Just, you know, things like little children's songs that you would get. I don't even remember. I was what you call a sporadic piano student. I was a good boy. It was considered … Mudsin said: I've got a nice lady's gonna teach you the piano. So I went to piano. And I liked, you know. But I was not…

225.t: Piano lessons at age seven or eight
225.s: His mother's idea; he studied by the book with the church organist for about two years.
225.q: My mother suggested it. It was my mother’s idea. In those days it was like a little bit of a, shall we say – da-da-da-dah – a status situation to have your child taking piano lessons, whether he wanted to or not. [laughter] I took piano lessons from this wonderful organist. I remember enjoying…

576.t: Singing grandparents, the cruel piano teacher and being teased for singing
576.s: Her drinking grandparents sang, her great aunt Alma hit her knuckles during piano lessons, and schoolmates teased her until she stopped singing.
576.q: Well, my grandfather always sang when he got drunk. And my grandmother played the piano, and my grandmother finally joined my grandfather in the drinking department, and she sang. So yeah, they were always singing. I could never understand. They were so happy and singing and lovey-dovey and…

460.t: The mellophone, Carl Owens and lessons about hard work
460.s: Laws ended up with the mellophone in elementary school, taught by the eccentric jazz pianist Carl Owens. He drifts into a lesson about hard work drawn from his tennis-playing son.
460.q: In elementary school they were offering instruments for the kids to select from. I just happened to get in on the last of the selection. So I ended up selecting the mellophone. A mellophone – in fact, I found out, when I was doing research on Freddie [Hubbard], when I taught – when I gave a…

226.t: Whether he ever left music; the piano was a family social thing
226.s: He insists he never left music and that the piano was bought for family socials, not his own ambition.
226.ch: Depression-era Chicago: jobs, marriage, first bands
226.q: I was always trying to do something in music, if it was playing the piano, which I wasn’t that great a piano player, enough to make a living out of that. So this was a hustle on the side of anything else that you would try to do.

589.t: 'Make the piano sing': Mendelsohn's lessons and gospel-classical roots
589.s: Mendelsohn raises his practice to hours a day and teaches him to make the piano sing; he decides to be a pianist and links his style to church and classical training.
589.q: being, that made me think that there’s something other than the brain, which memorizes 2 times 2 is 4 and Abraham Lincoln and history and all that stuff. That was the world, physically, physical and mental. You play baseball, and you memorize your tables. That’s it. You memorize music, and you do…

104.t: What draws her to the piano
104.s: She cannot explain the attraction beyond the melody of her mother's Chopin waltz; she loved playing by ear and also enjoyed gardening with her father, and Williams speaks of the piano's orchestral range.
104.ch: Jazz records, vaudeville and starting out
104.q: I can’t honestly . . . It was just something that seemed so . . . Well, first of all, the melody sticks in my head to this day. I remember what she played. The one . . . she played several, but the one that she played a lot was this one Chopin waltz. I don’t remember thinking, “Well, I’d love to do…

109.t: Stepfather refuses piano lessons; playing the church pump organ
109.s: He wanted piano lessons but his stepfather saw it as wasted money, so he played the church pump organ by ear; he left home after school out of disgust.
109.q: No. I hadn't chosen my instrument, really. I wanted to play the piano, but the piano lessons were so expensive and we didn't have much money, so I knew my stepfather would never consent to giving me piano lessons, because he didn't understand, you know.

113.t: Church songs and faking sickness to play the piano
113.s: He played church music at Sunday school and feigned illness to play the piano at home alone until a neighbor gave him away; his grandmother let him play other music.
113.q: Told my folks. And you know, my folks don't want me playing it no way. So I just didn't do any playing to speak of with the exception of every once in a while, well, I would play in the church, you know, play church music, but I wasn't reading any music, but, you know, you go to church and you hear…

70.t: Early piano: mother's Etude, prodigy at four, disliked lessons
70.s: His mother played piano, he played in church at four, took lessons from several teachers but disliked exercises and learned by ear and school singing.
70.ch: Childhood and first bands in Ohio
70.q: And she used to get the Etude every month and she played a little light classics. And so I used to crawl upon the stool behind her and play what I heard her

233.s: Buddy began playing the house piano before Monk took up bass, without any lessons; Monk secretly tried it with no result.
233.q: Yeah. Buddy just, it came very natural for Buddy. Because I remember when Buddy went to the army. He went to the army; before going to the army, I used to...I was always amazed by that. And that was before I started playing. Buddy and I wasn't, like I said, never really hung out and I'm... later I…

566.t: Singing at the piano as a small child and early lessons
566.s: Her mother sang in the choir and played piano at home while Humes sang along. Humes sang at church concerts at three or four, had a German teacher and then a lady teacher, and stopped lessons early. John Hammond later advised her against voice study.
566.q: She used to play the piano at home and she would teach me, you know? I would sit there and sing and she would play. I guess that's the way I got started singing.

385.t: Piano by ear, singing and playing together, early repertoire
385.s: He played only the black keys by ear, could sing and play at once, which got him into the Cats and the Fiddle, and did Fats Waller and Cab Calloway tunes as a kid.
385.q: I could only play in the black keys & it was all by ear. I never took a lesson in my life. I just could hear what was right & what was wrong. And that's the only

148.t: Summary of his musical life before Boyd
148.s: He sums up his pre-Boyd years: told he would be a doctor, his mother's teaching, listening to the moderns, and finding no teacher.
148.q: I would say to describe my musical life before joining Boyd that it was one in which I had been told that I was going to be in medicine, I was going to become a doctor, which I didn't doubt, I just accepted blindly and one of feeling musical stirrings in me, recognizing that I had an appetite for…

95.t: First singing and piano lessons in Houston
95.s: Wallace has sung since childhood in church and played piano from about age eight, taught by her brother; her parents were not musical.
95.q: I have been singing all my life, ever since I can remember. We sang at home in Houston, Texas, in church. And I'm 80 years old, so I've been singing 80 years back, I was in the church. I started off singing in the church.

388.t: Aunt Marion starts him on piano
388.s: Missing a mother's love but well cared for, Leeman starts piano at six or seven with his aunt and longs for drums, using his uncle's practice pad and homemade xylophone.
388.q: As a child, I missed a mother's love, living with older people, my grandfolks, but I was treated beautifully and I had good schooling. I was never hungry. And my aunt took an interest -- she's still living, she's 91, she's an old maid.

19.t: Banging the piano every evening and discovering chords
19.s: He rushes home daily to the piano and finds that stacking keys gives the harmonies his mother used to sing.
19.q: But from that day on, it was every day at the piano. School started about two-three weeks from there. And I remember when I went to school I could hardly wait to get back

86.t: Learning organ and piano with no formal teacher
86.s: Edison started on the pump organ, then piano, practising before school while balancing farm chores.
86.q: One of the old pump organs. Remember the old organs you used to pump with your feet? Yeah. Then my ant played organ in church and I finally played organ good enough to play in Sunday School. Then I played piano.
